ing: such as snapper or catfish, cut in chunks
st: Season the fish with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and set aside.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for [[4 minutes]] until soft.
Add the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] ginger, black pepper and nutmeg. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chili and cook for 5 minutes until they soften.
Pour in [[5 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the fish chunks gently. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Taste and add salt or more chili. Stir in the basil if using and serve hot.
Season the chicken and fish with [[1 tsp]] salt. Keep the fish in the fridge.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for [[5 minutes]].
Add the tomatoes and chili and cook 8 minutes until thick.
Add the chicken and [[3 cups]] water. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cassava, plantains and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer covered for 20 minutes until the cassava is almost tender.
Nestle in the fish chunks and simmer 8 minutes until cooked and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Taste, add salt, remove the chili and serve in bowls.
Put the cassava and plantains in a pot with [[4 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25 minutes until both are very soft when pierced.
Remove any tough woody cassava core. Drain, saving the cooking water.
Mash in a large bowl or pound with a wooden pestle, adding a splash of the hot cooking water as needed.
Keep working with a sturdy spoon for 5 to 8 minutes until smooth, stretchy and free of lumps.
Wet your hands and shape into smooth balls. Serve warm with soup or stew.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt. Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot for [[5 minutes]], then add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until soft.
Return the chicken with [[2.5 cups]] water, the chili and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of hot broth until smooth and stir it in.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chili and serve with rice or fufu.
Cut the ends off the plantains and slit the peel lengthwise. Peel it away.
Slice the plantains on a slant into pieces about 0.5 inch thick.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat until a slice sizzles right away.
Fry in a single layer, without crowding, for 2 to 3 minutes until golden brown on the bottom.
Flip and fry 2 minutes more until deep golden and caramelized at the edges.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with [[0.25 tsp]] salt if you like, and serve hot.
